name: OvertureMaps/overturemaps-py
what_it_holds: Official Overture Maps Foundation Python CLI (MIT license, 266 stars, 270 commits). Downloads Overture data for a bbox/region and a theme (places, buildings, transportation, divisions, base, addresses) and converts to GeoParquet/GeoJSON/etc. Places theme covers global POIs including accommodation/lodging categories (confirmed via schema repo cross-check, exact category list not extracted). Data underneath lives on S3/Azure as versioned monthly releases (STAC catalog), so pulling the same bbox at different Overture release dates gives a point-in-time-ish hotel/lodging POI count by city or metro.
why_useful: This is the practical one-command tool to actually pull the places theme (hotels/lodging category) for named cities/regions and diff across releases — turns the Overture places theme (row above) into something the team can script without hand-rolling Parquet/S3 access.

name: diegoantognini/HotelRec
what_it_holds: ~50 million TripAdvisor hotel reviews (paper claims this is the largest public hotel-review corpus), far larger than the 515k Booking.com Kaggle set we already hold. Each record: hotel URL, author, review DATE, overall rating, title, text, and sub-ratings (sleep quality, value, rooms, service, cleanliness, location). Repo has loader/preprocessing code; actual JSON data is hosted off-GitHub at https://drive.switch.ch/index.php/s/n48smsdufhRA7fR (academic-research-only licence, no commercial redistribution). 73 stars, last updated Jun 2026 (repo maintained), underlying data collected pre-2020 per README sample (earliest sample review 2010; full date range not stated in README).
why_useful: Dated per-hotel reviews at massive scale are the closest open substitute for a review-velocity/occupancy-nowcast panel (gap #2 realised occupancy proxy, and this scout's core theme) — review counts by date and hotel could be aggregated into a review-velocity time series by city/country as a hotel-demand proxy, the same logic as our reviews-based Airbnb 'stays index'. Caveat: appears to be a static historical crawl (not continuously updated), so its usefulness is as a backtest/calibration set for review-velocity-as-demand methodology, not a live feed; and licence is academic-only.
license: unspecified in README; explicit 'academic research purpose only' restriction

name: strr (UPGo McGill)

name: earnings-vol-study
